title: Camera focus speed: 0.3 s / 20 a second against 0.1 s / every frame
intro: tests/midi/03_band.mid, 0-34 s, alto sax on channel 1 sung by Delay Lama (profile mode), the band 6 dB down as live (live.wav). Both replay the same scripted camera move recorded from the 3D scene (before_scene/ and after_scene/: focus_timeline.csv and PNGs): camera 1A until 16 s, a glide in to the choir (16-19.6 s), held until 24.4 s, a glide back out (24.4-28 s), 1A from 28 s. 'Before' eases the focus offsets with a 0.3 s time constant and sends at most 20 a second (a 12 dB cut took about 0.7 s to reach 90 %); 'after' uses 0.1 s and sends every frame at 60 frames a second (about 0.23 s). The camera glides here rather than cutting, so the difference is how closely the levels follow it: 'before' still trails at 26.8 s (offsets of a few tenths of a dB left), 'after' is back at 0 dB. Strength 100 % in both, so the levels while held are the same (choir +6, bass, guitar and pad -21, drums -2.1 dB). No clipping in either.

tests.title: Camera focus: how fast the levels follow the camera
tests.question: Do the levels follow the camera fast enough now, without clicks or pumping?
tests.notes: Loop 14-30 s to hear the move in and out in each.
